text:
ryan-s: Escalation from AcmeCorp — customer says refund didn't go through. API responded 200 but the function call ended up invoking project_log_event (logger) instead of refund_processor. Request and logs attached.

anya: Can you paste the original request body and the tool-call assertion from logs?

ryan-s: Here — request body:
```json
POST /v1/call
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-infer",
  "input": "Issue: customer wants refund for order 12345",
  "functions": [
    {"name": "refund_processor", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"order_id": {"type":"string"}, "amount": {"type":"number"}}}},
    {"name": "project_log_event", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message": {"type":"string"}}}}
  ],
  "max_tokens": 256
}
```

ryan-s: Router log (excerpt):
```text
[router] fuzzy-match scores: refund_processor=0.47, project_log_event=0.89
[router] selected=project_log_event (score 0.89)
[invoker] invoked project_log_event args:{"message":"Refund attempted for order 12345 amount: \"100.00\""}
```

joel-k: That looks like schema shadowing — refund_processor.amount is number but model returned string "100.00" so fuzzy match favored project_log_event which had looser signature. Repro steps?

ryan-s: Repro steps I used:
1) Send payload above with amount as string
2) Observe router selection
3) project_log_event invoked and returned 200
4) refund_processor never called and no billing action taken

sam-ml: Two failure modes: if refund_processor had stricter validation it would have rejected earlier and we could fallback. Since logger accepted any string, router preferred higher confidence. We need to adjust signature priorities and add deterministic tie-breaker.

anya: Also saw that earlier the refund tool had a transient auth 401 (logs at 10:12:03) for that customer — could have degraded scoring? Any auth errors around same time?

ryan-s: Good call — logs:
```text
[refund_service] 10:12:03 401 Unauthorized KMS token expired for tenant acme-678
[refund_service] 10:12:04 500 downstream timeout
```

ryan-s: So sequence: refund tool briefly failing -> model returned string amount -> router fuzzy-match favored logger -> customer saw success 200 but no refund -> billing discrepancy.

joel-k: Mitigation: 1) Update refund_processor schema to coerce/accept numeric strings OR add explicit schema param types with required fields. 2) Change routing rules to prefer tools with 'financial' tag when intent contains refund keywords. 3) Add runtime check: if selected tool is non-financial but intent matches finance, log warning + fallback to manual review.

sam-ml: For immediate customer fix we should manually trigger refund and issue apology. I'll create a ticket. Also add a quick patch to prefer exact-type matches over fuzzy when confidence < 0.6.

ops-bot: scheduled runbook trigger created: #ticket-4521

anya: I'll PR schema change for refund_processor to accept numeric strings and add example unit tests.

ryan-s: Thanks — I'll contact customer and confirm manual refund processed. Recording repro and remediation steps here for the incident postmortem.

sam-ml: Add an alert when a tool is selected that is not in the expected domain (e.g., logger picked for payment flows).

ryan-s: noted. closing thread once ticket done :thumbsup:
